read.sections.0.heading.back: Jobs and transport draw people in

read.sections.0.text.note: "urbanisation" is การขยายตัวของเมือง (KEY_TERMS). Thai has one word, เมือง, for both "towns" and "cities"; "towns and cities" is mostly just เมือง, and the glossary definition says เมืองใหญ่และเมืองเล็ก.
read.sections.0.text.source: Most cities start small. A town often grows when something brings new jobs, such as a harbour, a railway or factories. Better transport also helps, because it lets people and goods move in and out more easily. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road and a cold-storage building opened, so fish could stay fresh all the way to the capital city. That created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview to do them. This kind of change is called urbanisation: more and more people come to live in towns and cities.
read.sections.0.text.back: Most cities start as small places. A small town often grows when something brings new jobs, such as a port, a railway or a factory. Better transport helps too, because it makes it easier for people and goods to come and go. Look at Bayview in Year 8. A new road and a cold-storage building opened, so fish could stay fresh all the way to the capital. This created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview for those jobs. This kind of change is called urbanisation: more and more people coming to live in cities.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: Most cities start small. A town can grow when new jobs come. A harbour, a railway or factories can bring jobs. Good transport helps people and goods move. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road opened. A big cold room opened too. It kept fish fresh. This made 800 new jobs. People moved to Bayview for the jobs. This is called urbanisation. More people live in towns and cities.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Most cities start small. A small town grows when there are new jobs. A port, a railway or a factory can bring jobs. Good transport helps people and things travel. Look at Bayview in Year 8. There is a new road and a big cold store. The cold store keeps fish fresh. So there are 800 new jobs. People move to Bayview to work. This is urbanisation: more people live in cities.

read.sections.1.heading.source: Real cities grew in similar ways
read.sections.1.heading.back: Real cities grow in similar ways

read.sections.1.text.note: Nairobi is ไนโรบี, Shenzhen is เซินเจิ้น (also written เซิ่นเจิ้น). "a special area for business" is เขตพิเศษสำหรับธุรกิจ (Thai textbooks say เขตเศรษฐกิจพิเศษ; the plainer words were kept).
read.sections.1.text.source: Many real cities grew in a similar way. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stop on a new railway. Workers and traders came, and the stop grew into a city. In 1980, only about 30,000 people lived in Shenzhen, in southern China. Then the government made it a special area for business. Factories opened, and millions of people moved there for work. Today it is one of the biggest cities in China. In both places, new jobs and transport made the population grow.
read.sections.1.text.back: Many real cities grew in similar ways. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stop on a new railway. Workers and traders came, and the stop grew into a city. In 1980 only about 30,000 people lived in Shenzhen in southern China. Then the government made it a special zone for business. Factories opened and millions of people moved there to work. Today Shenzhen is one of China's biggest cities. In both places, new jobs and transport made the population grow.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Real cities grew like this too. Nairobi is a big city in Kenya. It started in 1899 as a stop on a railway. Workers and traders came. The stop grew into a city. Shenzhen is a city in China. In 1980, it was small. Then many factories opened there. Millions of people came to work. Now it is one of China's biggest cities. In both places, jobs and transport made the population grow.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Real cities grow like this too. Nairobi is a city in Kenya. In 1899 Nairobi was a train stop. Workers and traders came. The stop grew into a city. Shenzhen is a city in China. In 1980 Shenzhen was still small. Then many factories opened. Millions of people came to work. Now Shenzhen is a very big city. In both places, jobs and transport made the population grow.

read.sections.2.text.note: "pressures" is แรงกดดัน, also in the heading, the write task and the speaking task. ปัญหา would be plainer but loses the idea of strain from growth.
read.sections.2.text.source: Growth can be good for a city, because a bigger city can have more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more homes, clean water and health care. A service is help that people need, like a clinic or a school. Infrastructure means the basic systems a place needs, such as roads, water pipes and power lines. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15, Bayview has new houses, a school and bus routes. But people wait a long time at the only clinic, because it did not grow as fast as the population. Good planners watch for pressures like this and plan ahead.
read.sections.2.text.back: Growth can be good for a city, because a bigger city has more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more homes, clean water and health care. Services are help people need, such as clinics or schools. Infrastructure means the basic systems a place must have, such as roads, water pipes and power lines. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15 Bayview has new homes, schools and bus lines, but people must wait a long time at the one clinic, because the clinic hasn't grown as fast as the population. Good planners watch for pressures like this and plan ahead.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: Growth can be good. A big city has more jobs, schools and buses. But more people need more things. They need homes and clean water. They need a service like a clinic. They need infrastructure, like roads and pipes. These take time to build. In Year 15, people wait a long time at the Bayview clinic. It did not grow as fast as the population. Planners try to see problems early.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: Growth can be good. A big city has more jobs, schools and buses. But more people need more things. They need homes and clean water. They need services like clinics. They need infrastructure such as roads and water pipes. These take time to build. In Year 15, the clinic in Bayview has long waits. The clinic didn't grow as fast as the population. Planners try to see problems early.

watch.summary.source: The video starts with a fact: today, more than half of all people live in towns and cities. About 10,000 years ago, people began to farm. They could grow food, so they stayed in villages. Later, better farming made extra food. Not everyone had to farm, so some people did other jobs. Villages grew into cities. Trade grew too, with carts, ships, roads and ports. Much later, factories and new machines helped cities grow even bigger. Cities added police, fire services, roads and ways to take away waste. In the future, even more people will live in cities. The video says cities must give everyone enough food, toilets and schools. They must also protect the land. Ideas include rooftop gardens, tall buildings, and power from the sun and wind.
watch.summary.back: The video starts with the fact that today more than half of the world's people live in cities. About 10,000 years ago people started farming. They could grow food, so they settled in villages. Later better farming gave leftover food. Not everyone had to farm, so some people did other work. Villages grew into cities. Trade grew too, with carts, boats, roads and ports. Much later, factories and new machines helped cities get even bigger. Cities added police, fire services, roads and ways to take rubbish away. In the future even more people will live in cities. The video says cities must have enough food, toilets and schools for everyone, and must protect the land too. Ideas include rooftop gardens, tall buildings and energy from sunlight and wind.
